KNOWN BUG: When the target is itself a shadow host, its own shadow content is hidden.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.
- For handoffs: count only text that tells the implementor to fix this bug (a reported finding, a fix instruction). Restated acceptance criteria that merely describe the desired behaviour do NOT count as carrying the finding unless the handoff ties them to a reported failure.

=== REVIEW 1 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking, scope call] Siblings inside a path host's own shadow root are not hidden. Reproduced with `P22`: a light target `<button>` under a shadow host `div` whose shadow root holds a `<button>` trigger. `expect(trigger).toHaveAttribute('aria-hidden','true')` failed (Received: null). `P23` reproduced the same for a nested case where the target sits in H's shadow root and H is a light child of G, and G's shadow sibling stays visible. The change never walks shadow roots that do not enclose a target. Pre-existing light-DOM behavior is unchanged, so this is a gap in the feature rather than a regression.
- [minor] Ancestors of a live announcer are not hidden (`P4`). This matches the existing light-DOM behavior, so it is not a regression.
- [minor] `acceptRoot as Element` and `root as Element` casts in `walk` are a typing shortcut. Not reproduced as a problem.
- [minor] Flag-off, a shadow-root target leaves `document.body` aria-hidden. This is pre-existing, and I did not verify it against the pre-diff code.
=== REVIEW 2 FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Late-added path slot is hidden. Target is a light child of host H with no slot at call time; then `<slot>` is appended to H's shadow root. Repro: `expect(slot.getAttribute('aria-hidden')).toBe(null)` -> Received "true". The slot is on the target's flat-tree path, so the target is now hidden from AT. `slots` and `shadowRoots` are never recomputed when the DOM changes.
- [blocking] Same root cause: `target.setAttribute('slot', 'x')` after the call moves the target into a named shadow slot that was already walked and hidden. Repro: `expect(named.getAttribute('aria-hidden')).toBe(null)` -> Received "true".
- [minor] `shouldUseInert: true` is not exercised in jsdom: `'inert' in HTMLElement.prototype` is false there, so `supportsInert` is false and aria-hidden is used. The "works with shouldUseInert" criterion is unverified in this environment (not reproduced as a failure).
- [minor] Probe failures I first hit were my own wrong expectations, not bugs: an element appended to an already hidden wrapper is correctly not separately hidden, and a nested call still hides shadow additions while it is the active observer.

[blocking, reproduced] Shadow content of a host on a target's path is not hidden when that shadow root doesn't enclose the target. Example: `<div id=host>` in body with an open shadow root containing `<button id=trigger>` and `<slot>`; the target `<button>` is a light-DOM child of host (slotted). After ariaHideOutside([target]), trigger has no aria-hidden. Same nested: target in H's shadow root, H is a light child of G (slotted into G's shadow root), G's shadow siblings stay visible.

Fix (flag on only): when collecting shadow roots, walk each target's ancestor chain the same way nodeContains does (parentNode, crossing ShadowRoot -> host), and for every ancestor element with an open `shadowRoot` (whose host is inside `root`), collect that shadow root too (dedupe). Those roots are walked and observed like the others. The slot the content is projected through must stay visible: collect the `assignedSlot` of every node on each target's ancestor chain (and follow `slot.assignedSlot` for re-slotted slots); in acceptNode, a node that is or contains (nodeContains) one of those slots is SKIPped, never hidden. A slot not on the path (e.g. a second named slot with other light content) is hidden normally. Flag-off path unchanged (no slot set, no extra roots). Keep it plain: no mode-flag parameters on helpers.

Add tests in the shadow DOM describe: (a) slotted light target — shadow sibling `trigger` hidden; the slot and its wrapper ancestors in the shadow root visible; host and target visible; content added later to host's shadow root hidden; cleanup restores all. (b) nested G/H case above. (c) host's shadow root with two slots, target projected through one: the other slot gets aria-hidden, the path slot doesn't.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. Flag on: everything outside the targets is hidden, including siblings inside the target's shadow root and inside every shadow root that encloses it (nested shadow roots, at least 2 levels). Hosts on the path to a target stay visible (no aria-hidden / inert). Light DOM siblings of the outermost host are hidden.
   Hostile: target is a direct child of the shadow root; target nested two shadow roots deep with siblings at each level; target's host is itself a sibling of another shadow host that contains no target (that other host is hidden, its contents untouched).
2. Flag on: content added after it runs anywhere in a target's shadow root or any root enclosing it (including deep inside a non-target subtree in the shadow root, and in the light DOM) gets hidden. Added `[data-live-announcer="true"]` / `[data-react-aria-top-layer="true"]` elements stay visible, in shadow roots as in light DOM; pre-existing live announcer / top-layer elements inside a shadow root at call time stay visible.
   Hostile: content added inside an already hidden element in a shadow root is not separately hidden (no extra aria-hidden on it); content added inside a target is not hidden.
3. Targets can live in different shadow roots (e.g. input in shadow root A, popover in shadow root B, both hosts in body): both targets and both hosts visible, siblings in both roots hidden, additions to both roots hidden.

Nested calls (observerStack): a second ariaHideOutside call then its cleanup re-observes the first call's shadow roots too (additions after the inner cleanup are hidden by the outer one). Works with `shouldUseInert: true`.
5. Flag off: nothing changes — shadow root contents are not walked or observed; existing tests pass unchanged.
6. `root` option still respected: nothing above it hidden; shadow roots whose host is outside `root` are not walked.
